me_boulderama.blurb: Boulderama is a small bouldering zone in Bath, one of three clusters near the Whiskeag Trail, within a short walk of a cemetery on the edge of town. Ledge and free-standing granite blocks sit beside a bike trail in the woods, and development there is recent. Thirteen problems are on record, running from V0 up to a V12 project, with a handful of friendly lines near the bottom, a middle group around V3 to V5, and a cluster of serious V8 problems for strong climbers. Expect a quiet, lightly developed spot rather than a destination circuit; bring pads and a spotter, and pair it with the neighbouring crag zones for a fuller session.

me_split_boulder_the.blurb: The Split Boulder is one of just two boulders that make up the tiny Two and a Half Bouldermen cluster inside Kenyon Hill Preserve in southern Maine. It stands in an open clearing beside the trail, so sun reaches it and the spot feels calm. Thirteen problems are recorded, from V0 to about V9, though most sit in the V2 to V4 band, with four at V4 and only a couple of harder lines. It suits a short session of moderate problems, ideally combined with the neighbouring boulder and the other blocks around the preserve.

me_monument_cove.blurb: Monument Cove is a seaside bouldering spot on the Acadia shoreline of Mount Desert Island, set in dramatic surroundings right at the water. A long vertical granite face holds plenty of easy problems, with a small roof at one end. Most of the twelve entries are boulder problems from V0 to V6, concentrated at the friendly end with a few mid-grade lines around V3 to V5, plus a single short trad line. Good for a relaxed session with a pad and a view, and a decent choice for newer boulderers. Because it sits at sea level, high water can swamp parts of the area, so check the tide first.

me_14_ocean_lookout_upper_megunticook.blurb: Ocean Lookout, also called the Upper Megunticook Cliffs, is a prominent cliff high in the Camden Hills above the coast. It sees fewer climbers than the other Camden crags, probably because of a long uphill hike of roughly a mile. The twelve routes are almost all trad, built around steep cracks from fist size to fingers, with one sport line. Grades start near 5.8 and run to 5.13, with a spread through the 5.9 to 5.12 range, so it suits experienced crack climbers who want solitude and views more than a quick roadside lap.
